USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Reducing an inflammatory precursor

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 35-year-old man with familial Mediterranean fever has recurrent inflammatory attacks and newly detected AA amyloid in a kidney biopsy. Which biological goal best explains why suppressing the underlying inflammatory disease can limit further amyloid formation?

  1. Reducing sustained serum amyloid A production
  2. Eliminating a clonal plasma-cell population
  3. Increasing beta-2 microglobulin synthesis
  4. Converting Congo red to an inactive dye
  5. Stimulating transthyretin tetramer dissociation
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Reducing sustained serum amyloid A production

Reducing inflammation lowers the supply of SAA, the precursor for AA fibrils. This targets new precursor production rather than instantly removing existing deposits.

Understanding the options

Reducing sustained serum amyloid A production
Reducing inflammation lowers the supply of SAA, the precursor for AA fibrils. This targets new precursor production rather than instantly removing existing deposits.
Eliminating a clonal plasma-cell population
That targets AL amyloidosis rather than AA.
Increasing beta-2 microglobulin synthesis
This would not reduce AA precursor and could worsen a different protein burden.
Converting Congo red to an inactive dye
Congo red is a diagnostic stain, not the cause of deposition.
Stimulating transthyretin tetramer dissociation
TTR destabilization concerns ATTR and does not reduce SAA.
